events.text: {npc} dares you to a race to the top of the old pine on the hill. Half the village children come to watch.

mem.note: beat me up the old pine in front of everyone

ok.log: You touch the top branch first. {npc} climbs down without a word and does not speak to you for a month.

fail.log: {npc} wins by a hand. {He} sits on the top branch and laughs until {he} nearly falls off.

mem.note: said racing was for children

effects.log: "Coward," says {npc}. The other children agree. You are, after all, a child.

variants: {npc} challenges you to race up the old pine on the hill. Half the children in the village turn out to watch.

events.text: At the martial exam in town, you see {npc} slip a bribe to the examiner's servant. The results go up tomorrow.

mem.note: exposed my bribe at the exam

effects.log: The examiner throws {npc} out. {He} looks back at you from the gate, and you know this is not over.

ok.log: Your name goes up above {npc}'s, bribe and all. That hurts {him} more than any accusation.

fail.log: {npc}'s name goes up above yours. You say nothing. You remember.

mem.note: kept my secret at the exam

effects.log: {npc} goes pale, then red. "Why didn't you tell them?" You shrug. {He} does not know what to do with that.

variants: The night before the martial exam results, you see {npc} in the alley behind the hall, pressing a purse into the hand of the examiner's servant.
At the town's martial exam, a servant of the examiner pockets something from {npc} with a practised hand. The lists go up in the morning.

events.text: At the Lantern Festival, {npc} ({npc_realm}) steps into the square and challenges you, loud enough for the whole town to hear.

mem.note: beat me at the Lantern Festival

ok.log: The crowd roars. {npc} picks {him}self up off the stones and swears you will pay for this.

fail.log: {npc} wins, and bows far too deeply. The whole town sees you lose.

mem.note: would not even fight me

effects.log: "Another year, perhaps." The crowd laughs, and not at you. {npc} storms off.

variants: In the middle of the Lantern Festival, {npc} ({npc_realm}) strides into the square and calls you out, loud enough to stop the music.
The lanterns are lit, the square is full, and {npc} ({npc_realm}) picks that moment to challenge you in front of the whole town.

events.text: {npc} has reached {npc_realm}, ahead of you. {He} comes to visit, just to be seen walking past your door.

mem.note: congratulated me when I passed them

effects.log: {npc} blinks. {He} expected anger. "...Thank you," {he} says, and means it.
That night you train until your hands bleed. Hunger is a kind of fuel.

choices.text: Spread a rumour about how {he} got there

mem.note: spread lies about how I reached my realm

effects.log: The rumour spreads well. {npc} finds out where it started.

variants: Word comes that {npc} has reached {npc_realm}, ahead of you. That afternoon {he} happens to stroll past your door, slowly, twice.
{npc} has broken through to {npc_realm} before you. {He} drops by with a gift of tea, mostly to stand in your doorway and be seen.

events.text: {npc} comes to you, pride in pieces. "How? How did you get so far ahead?"

mem.note: taught me when they could have gloated

effects.log: You spend a season training together. {npc} breaks through soon after. Something between you changes.

mem.note: laughed at me when I asked for help

effects.log: {npc} leaves without a word. Somewhere, a grudge takes root.

events.text: A messenger finds you: {npc} has been ambushed on the mountain road by enemies of {his} sect. {He} will not last the night alone.

mem.note: saved my life on the mountain road

ok.log: You arrive at the worst moment and turn it. {npc}, bleeding, stares at you. "You came. Why did you come?"

fail.deathCause: an ambush meant for your rival

mem.note: nearly died trying to save me

fail.log: You both barely escape. {npc} carries you the last mile.

effects.log: {npc} survives, somehow. {He} hears that you knew, and did not come.

variants: A breathless runner brings word: {npc} was caught on the mountain road by enemies of {his} sect and is holding them off alone. {He} will not see morning without help.
The message is three words scrawled on a scrap: {npc}, ambushed, mountain road. Whoever sent it did not stay to say more. {He} will not last the night alone.

events.text: A letter surfaces in the magistrate's office, accusing you of dealing with the Demonic Cult. The handwriting is disguised. You know whose it is: {npc}.

mem.note: turned my letter back on me

ok.log: You find the scribe {npc} paid. The scandal falls on {him} instead.

fail.log: The accusation sticks for a season. Friends stop visiting. {npc} is seen smiling.

mem.note: beat me in my own courtyard

ok.log: You walk into {npc}'s courtyard and leave {him} on the ground. The letters stop.

fail.log: {npc} was ready for you. You crawl home.

events.text: {npc} arrives with a jar of old wine and two cups. "All these years I measured myself against you. I think I would rather stand beside you."

choices.text: Swear brotherhood under the peach trees

mem.note: swore brotherhood with me

effects.log: Two rivals, one oath. The murim hears of it and does not quite believe it.

choices.text: "A rival is more useful than a friend"

effects.log: {npc} laughs. "Then keep running. I'll be right behind you."

events.text: You and {npc} have both fallen for the same person, the magistrate's daughter who reads poetry in the plum garden.

mem.note: won the heart I wanted

ok.log: She chooses your poem. {npc} tears {his} own into pieces and throws them in the pond.

fail.log: She chooses {npc}'s poem. {He} is a gracious winner, which is somehow worse.

mem.note: stepped aside for me

effects.log: "Why?" asks {npc}. You don't answer. {He} never forgets it.

events.text: You and {npc} have both fallen for the same person, the magistrate's son who reads poetry in the plum garden.

mem.note: won the heart I wanted

ok.log: He chooses your poem. {npc} tears {his} own into pieces and throws them in the pond.

fail.log: He chooses {npc}'s poem. {He} is a gracious winner, which is somehow worse.

mem.note: stepped aside for me

effects.log: "Why?" asks {npc}. You don't answer. {He} never forgets it.

variants: It turns out you and {npc} have lost your hearts to the same person: the magistrate's son, who reads poetry in the plum garden.

events.text: A letter in a hand you have known since childhood: "The peak of Mount Hua. The first full moon of autumn. One of us should finally know." {npc}, {npc_realm}, is waiting.

mem.note: beat me on the peak of Mount Hua, and let me live

ok.log: Two hundred exchanges under the moon. When {npc} falls, you lower your sword. {He} laughs, and for the first time in many years, {he} sounds happy. "So that's what it takes."

fail.deathCause: your rival {npc}, on the peak of Mount Hua
fail.log: {npc} wins. {He} stands over you a long moment, then sheathes {his} sword. "Not like this," {he} says, and carries you down the mountain.

mem.note: never came to Mount Hua

effects.log: {npc} waits on the peak for three nights. Then {he} comes down, and never speaks your name again.

events.text: {npc} is old now, like you. {He} sits beside you on a bench overlooking the village where you both grew up.

mem.note: laughed with me about the old days

effects.log: "I was sure I would beat you at everything," {npc} says. "Everything I became, I became chasing you."
{npc} thinks for a long time. "Neither of us. Both of us. Pass the wine."

events.text: {npc}'s best disciple challenges you in public, at {his} master's secret urging.

mem.note: went easy on my disciple

ok.log: You disarm the youth without a scratch and give back the sword. {npc} watches from the crowd, arms folded.

fail.log: The disciple is better than you thought. {npc} is insufferable for a year.

mem.note: told my disciple to send me instead

effects.log: The whole town hears it. So does {npc}.
